standard_prerequisites.name: Finiteness of the number of irreducible components of an etale neighbourhood
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Decent Spaces, the definition of a decent space and the lemma that the generic points of an etale neighbourhood map to the generic point of the space
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the finiteness of the number of generic points of the affine neighbourhood, hence of its minimal primes.

standard_prerequisites.name: Decomposition of a normal ring with finitely many minimal primes
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, the lemma characterizing a reduced ring as a product of domains indexed by its minimal primes, applied to a normal ring
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the decomposition of the ring of the neighbourhood into a product of normal domains.

core_obligations: Choose an affine neighbourhood (proof lines 523-528): take an affine scheme U with an etale morphism to the space and with the given point in its image; the generic points of the irreducible components of U map to the generic point of the space, so by decency their number is finite.
Decompose the ring (proof lines 528-532): writing U as the spectrum of a ring A, the ring is normal with finitely many minimal primes, hence a product of the normal domains attached to those primes.

Conclude (proof lines 532-534): the neighbourhood decomposes as a disjoint union of the spectra of those normal domains, and the given point lies in the image of one of them, which is a normal integral affine scheme etale over the space.
proof_roadmap: Use decency to bound the number of irreducible components of an affine etale neighbourhood.
Decompose the normal ring of that neighbourhood into a product of normal domains.
Pick the component through which the given point is reached.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a normal integral algebraic space and a point of it there is a normal integral affine scheme with an etale morphism to the space having the point in its image (statement lines 516-521). The proof (proof lines 523-536) uses decency to make the number of irreducible components of an affine etale neighbourhood finite, decomposes the normal ring of that neighbourhood into a product of normal domains, and picks the component through which the point is reached. H2: a three-step argument with two inputs, written out in full.
